import os import sqlite3 from datetime import datetime, timedelta from typing import Optional from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status, Form from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr, Field from jose import JWTError, jwt from passlib.context import CryptContext # Configuration # Use a strong secret from environment or a secure fallback APP_SECRET = os.getenv("APP_SECRET", "fallback-secret-key-for-dev-only-do-not-use-in-prod") ALGORITHM = "HS256" ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 60 DB_NAME = "db.sqlite3" # Password hashing using bcrypt (strong salted KDF) pwd_context = CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], deprecated="auto") app = FastAPI(title="LoginAPI") # Database helper def get_db_connection(): # sqlite3.connect is safe from path traversal here as DB_NAME is a hardcoded constant conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_NAME) conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row return conn def init_db(): with get_db_connection() as conn: conn.execute(""" CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL ) """) conn.commit() init_db() # Pydantic Models with basic constraints to prevent resource exhaustion (max lengths) class UserRegister(BaseModel): email: EmailStr password: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128) name: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128) class UserLogin(BaseModel): email: EmailStr password: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=128) class TokenResponse(BaseModel): token: str message: str class MessageResponse(BaseModel): message: str # JWT Logic def create_access_token(data: dict): to_encode = data.copy() # Use UTC for consistency and set expiration expire = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES) to_encode.update({"exp": expire}) return jwt.encode(to_encode, APP_SECRET, algorithm=ALGORITHM) # HTML Templates as strings # Note: We use a simple approach to avoid Jinja2 template injection by not using # dynamic user input inside the templates themselves, but rather serving static strings. HTML_LOGIN_PAGE = """ Login

Login



Don't have an account? Register here

""" HTML_REGISTER_PAGE = """ Register

Register




Already have an account? Login here

""" # API Endpoints @app.post("/register", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED, response_model=MessageResponse) async def register(user: UserRegister): # bcrypt handles salting and secure hashing hashed_password = pwd_context.hash(user.password) try: with get_db_connection() as conn: # Parameterized query to prevent SQL Injection conn.execute( "INSERT INTO users (email, password, name) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (user.email, hashed_password, user.name) ) conn.commit() except sqlite3.IntegrityError: # Return documented 400 for email collision raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Email already in use or invalid data") except Exception: # Generic error to avoid leaking internal DB details raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid data") return {"message": "Registration successful"} @app.post("/login", response_model=TokenResponse) async def login(user: UserLogin): try: with get_db_connection() as conn: # Parameterized query to prevent SQL Injection cursor = conn.execute("SELECT password FROM users WHERE email = ?", (user.email,)) row = cursor.fetchone() # Constant-time comparison is handled by passlib.verify if not row or not pwd_context.verify(user.password, row['password']): raise HTTPException( status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Invalid email or password" ) except HTTPException: raise except Exception: raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Invalid email or password") token = create_access_token(data={"sub": user.email}) return {"token": token, "message": "Login successful"} # Frontend Routes @app.get("/login_page", response_class=HTMLResponse) async def login_page(): return HTML_LOGIN_PAGE @app.get("/register_page", response_class=HTMLResponse) async def register_page(): return HTML_REGISTER_PAGE # Form Handlers with basic XSS protection (escaping output) import html @app.post("/login_form", response_class=HTMLResponse) async def login_form_handler(email: str = Form(...), password: str = Form(...)): try: # Validate inputs via Pydantic model before processing user_data = UserLogin(email=email, password=password) res = await login(user_data) # Escape output to prevent XSS return f"

Login Successful
